extracted.intended_audience: heads of executive departments and agencies, agency rulewriters and regulatory staff, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) officials
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for Federal agencies when proposing, promulgating, and budgeting for new regulations under Executive Order 13771 (Reducing Regulation and Controlling Regulatory Costs). Covers identification of offsetting repeals, cost caps/allowances, reporting to OMB, and related implementation guidance and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy of prudent financial responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the executive branch to be prudent and financially responsible in the expenditure of funds, and to manage the costs associated with the governmental imposition of private expenditures required to comply with Federal regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should manage regulatory costs through a budgeting process and seek to control planned regulation costs as part of executive-branch policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify at least two existing regulations to repeal when issuing a new regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an executive department or agency publicly proposes for notice and comment or otherwise promulgates a new regulation, it shall identify at least two existing regulations to be repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement applies at the time of public proposal or other promulgation; identification of candidate repeals must be part of the agency's regulatory planning for the new rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero net incremental cost requirement (FY2017)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fiscal year 2017, the heads of all agencies are directed that the total incremental cost of all new regulations, including repealed regulations, to be finalized this year shall be no greater than zero, unless otherwise required by law or consistent with written advice from the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to FY2017; exceptions exist where otherwise required by law or where the OMB Director provides written advice allowing otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: New incremental costs must be offset by elimination of existing costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new incremental costs associated with new regulations shall, to the extent permitted by law, be offset by the elimination of existing costs associated with at least two prior regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any agency eliminating existing costs under this subsection shall do so in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act and other applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Director to provide implementation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall provide the heads of agencies with guidance on implementation, addressing processes for standardizing the measurement and estimation of regulatory costs; standards for determining what qualifies as new and offsetting regulations; standards for determining the costs of existing regulations considered for elimination; accounting for costs in different fiscal years; oversight methods for offsets across times or agencies; and circumstances justifying waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance must cover measurement/estimation methods, qualification standards for offsetting regulations, cross-fiscal-year accounting methods, oversight approaches, emergency/waiver criteria, and phasing in/updating requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify offsets and estimate costs/savings in Regulatory Plans (beginning FY2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with the Regulatory Plans for fiscal year 2018, and for each fiscal year thereafter, the head of each agency shall identify, for each regulation that increases incremental cost, the offsetting regulations described in section 2(c), and provide the agency's best approximation of the total costs or savings associated with each new regulation or repealed regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must include best approximations (estimates) of total costs or savings for both new and repealed regulations in their Regulatory Plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Director-approved regulations in the Unified Regulatory Agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: Each regulation approved by the Director during the Presidential budget process shall be included in the Unified Regulatory Agenda required under Executive Order 12866.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations approved during the Presidential budget process must appear on the Agenda; this supports transparency and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on issuing regulations not on the latest Unified Regulatory Agenda (unless exempted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise required by law, no regulation shall be issued by an agency if it was not included on the most recent version or update of the published Unified Regulatory Agenda, unless the issuance of such regulation was approved in advance in writing by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must either include regulations on the most recent Agenda or obtain prior written approval from the Director to issue them; statutory requirements override this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director to set agency-specific total incremental cost allowances annually
rubrics_metrics.description: During the Presidential budget process, the Director shall identify to agencies a total amount of incremental costs that will be allowed for each agency in issuing new regulations and repealing regulations for the next fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No regulations exceeding the agency's total incremental cost allowance will be permitted in that fiscal year, unless required by law or approved in writing by the Director. The allowance may allow an increase or require a reduction in total regulatory cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'regulation' and listed exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this order the term 'regulation' or 'rule' means an agency statement of general or particular applicability and future effect designed to implement, interpret, or prescribe law or policy or to describe the procedure or practice requirements of an agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition expressly excludes: (a) regulations issued with respect to a military, national security, or foreign affairs function; (b) regulations related to agency organization, management, or personnel; and (c) any other category of regulations exempted by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with applicable law and appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation must not conflict with statutes or funding limitations; agencies must follow other legal requirements when carrying out the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order does not alter statutory authority or Director functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect: (i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or (ii) the functions of the Director relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that the EO does not supersede or lessen preexisting statutory authorities or OMB Director functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order does not create enforceable private rights
rubrics_metrics.description: This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals or entities cannot assert private causes of action based solely on this order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to follow APA and other applicable law when eliminating existing regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agency eliminating existing costs associated with prior regulations under this order shall do so in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act and other applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeal actions used to realize offsets must comply with notice-and-comment and other statutory procedural requirements as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director discretion for exemptions, waivers, phasing, and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may exempt other categories of regulations, provide written advice permitting deviations, consider phasing in and updating requirements, and identify emergencies and other circumstances that might justify individual waivers of requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direction anticipates Director-level discretion to define exemptions, grant waivers for emergencies, phase implementation, and update standards over time; such actions are to be documented in Director guidance or written approvals.
